title: Rights and Risks Alignment Manual
author: Sana Iqbal
content:
Overview:
This manual defines a single, company‑wide pattern for aligning access and permissions, change approvals, data handling expectations, procurement thresholds, vendor risk decisions, and travel expense governance. It is intended for stakeholders who approve access, manage vendor relationships, run platform changes, or sign off on spend.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems.
- Covers systems managed by Hosted, Dedicated and Private teams (internal and customer environments).
- Does NOT replace team‑specific operational runbooks; instead it provides the canonical authorization and risk model teams should import into local procedures.

Principles (short):
1) Least privilege by default: grant the minimum role required for 90% of daily work.
2) Segregation of duties: approval chains must separate requesters from approvers for critical actions.
3) Risk‑based accuracy: higher risk assets require stronger controls (2FA, approved devices, KMS‑wrapped keys).
4) Single source for approvals: use the Company Access Portal (CAP) for all access requests and the Procurement Portal for spend.

Authorization tiers (table described):
- Tier 1 — Low impact: read access to public/internal docs, non‑prod dashboards. Approver: Manager. Review cadence: annual.
- Tier 2 — Operational: write access to non‑production systems, basic production monitoring. Approver: Service Owner + Manager. Review cadence: quarterly.
- Tier 3 — Sensitive: production write, secret access (API keys, DB write), vendor integrations. Approver: Service Owner + Security Reviewer + Finance (if cost). Review cadence: monthly.
- Tier 4 — Elevated: access to PII/regulated datasets, KMS key material, ability to deploy to customer VPCs. Approver: Exec Sponsor + Security + Legal + Finance. Review cadence: monthly; emergency access requires post‑hoc audit.

Access request workflow (numbered):
1) Initiate request in CAP with: requester, justification, scope, required duration (one‑off, 30/90/365 days or indefinite with quarterly review), and risk assessment answers.
2) Manager auto-approves for Tier 1 within 48 hrs.
3) For Tier 2–4, the approval chain is auto-notified; approvers have 72 hrs to respond.
4) If an approver rejects, the request returns to requester with required changes.
5) After approval, IAM issues the entitlement and records the change in the Audit Ledger (immutable entry with request id).
6) Access is time‑boxed; expiration triggers an automated review reminder 7 days before expiry.

Change management summary (SRE + platform integration):
- All planned production changes must use the Change Request (CR) flow in the Change Registry and follow these thresholds:
  - Routine (low‑risk): config tweaks, non‑customer facing infra changes. Owner to notify on-call and deploy. Post‑deploy review within 48 hrs.
  - Standard (medium): schema changes, scaling policies, model rollout to staging. Requires peer review, safety smoke tests, canary percent <= 5% for 24 hours.
  - Major (high): API contract changes, data migrations, model rollouts to production >5% traffic, or infra upgrades that impact SLA. Requires CR with approvals: Service Owner, Eng SRE, Security, Product, and Finance for cost > $10k.
- Change freeze windows: last 3 business days of every quarter and major release dates (documented on Team Roadmaps).
- Emergency changes: Follow the Emergency CR path — immediate approver notification by PagerDuty; postmortem required within 5 business days.

Data classification and handling (short table style):
- Public: documentation intended for external consumption. Storage: general bucket, no restrictions.
- Internal: company internal docs, non‑sensitive metrics. Storage: corporate GCS/Azure Blob with standard encryption at rest.
- Confidential: customer non‑PII, non‑regulated business data. Access: Tier 3 controls, logged, KMS for secrets.
- Restricted: PII, regulated customer data, HIPAA/CCPA scope. Access: Tier 4, strict RBAC, HSM/KMS, network segmentation (VPCs), mandatory audit logging and quarterly attestation.

Data handling rules (bullets):
- All restricted data must be stored in approved environments only (see Appendix: Approved Data Stores).
- Export of confidential or restricted data outside Redwood requires Data Owner + Legal + Security approval and an executed DPA if third‑party.
- Backups containing restricted data must use customer‑segregated keys and have a retention policy consistent with the customer's contract.

Procurement and expenses (approval thresholds):
- Micro Purchases: <= $1,000 — Manager approval in Procurement Portal.
- Standard Purchases: $1,001–$25,000 — Manager + Finance approval; procurement handles vendor setup.
- Strategic Purchases: $25,001–$250,000 — Manager + Finance + Legal + Procurement Sourcing; requires vendor risk assessment.
- Enterprise/Capital: > $250,000 — Executive sponsor + VP Finance + Legal + Procurement; board notification for multiyear commitments > $1M.
- POs: All purchases > $5,000 require a PO.
- Expense submissions: employees must attach receipts in the Expense Portal within 60 days. Per‑diem rates are published separately; use corporate cards for travel when possible.

Vendor management and risk tiers:
- Low (L): SaaS with no customer data access (e.g., marketing SaaS). Controls: standard contract, annual review.
- Medium (M): Vendors that process internal non‑sensitive operational data or limited customer metadata. Controls: SOC2 or equivalent, annual contract review, standard DPA.
- High (H): Vendors with access to PII, regulated data, or that run inside customer‑facing infrastructure. Controls: SOC2 + contractual SLAs, penetration test report, annual on‑site/in‑depth review, segmentation verification.

Vendor onboarding checklist (condensed):
1) Business Owner submits Vendor Intake form in Procurement Portal.
2) Procurement runs vendor questionnaire + basic risk scoring.
3) Security reviews for High/Medium vendors.
4) Legal negotiates contracts and DPAs.
5) Finance approves payment terms and wiring details.
6) IAM and Service Owner configure minimal access and set review cadence.

Travel and expense governance (key bullets):
- All travel must be pre‑approved in Travel Portal with estimated cost line‑items.
- Employees must use company travel vendors when available to ensure insurance and duty‑of‑care.
- Per‑diem: domestic US $75/day, international rates follow the country band table in HR. Exceptions require manager + people‑ops signoff.
- Business class travel requires VP approval for flights >8 hours.
- Travel insurance: company buys standard travel insurance for employees on international trips over 7 days.

- Monthly Access Review Checklist (CSV export): [CONFLUENCE LINK]/access-review-checklist

Ownership and roles (short list):
- IAM Team: entitlement execution, audit ledger maintenance.
- Security: risk reviewer for Tier 3–4 access, vendor security assessments, incident response.
- Procurement: vendor intake, license negotiation, PO issuance.
- Finance: purchase approval, budget checks, expense reimbursements.
- Legal: contract and DPA review/approval.
- Service Owner: approves service specific access and changes, owns runbook.

Escalation matrix (condensed):
- For access denials or suspicious activity: report to Service Owner -> Security -> Head of Security within 1 hour for P1 incidents.
- For procurement delays > 10 business days on critical purchases: notify Procurement Lead -> VP Finance.

Monitoring and audits:
- Quarterly access recertification for Tier 3–4.
- Annual vendor risk re‑assessment for Medium and High vendors.
- Change registry audit every month for auditability and SLI reporting.

Appendix: sample access request (YAML example)
---
request_id: ARC-2027-0123
requester: "james.wu@redwood.com"
service: "model-serving-prod"
requested_role: "db_writer"
justification: "Urgent data fix for customer billing discrepancy"
duration_days: 7
risk_answers:
  - handles_customer_pii: false
  - deploys_production: true
  - needs_kms_access: false
approvals_required: ["Manager", "Service Owner", "Security"]
---

Governance notes and next steps:
- This manual will be the canonical reference for companywide approvals. Teams must not create parallel approval matrices that diverge from these thresholds without a documented exception and Executive signoff.
- Quarterly review of these thresholds will be owned by the Operations Governance Council (Procurement + Security + Finance + People‑Ops).
